answers.answer:
The term “Civilization Zero” (or “Type 0 Civilization”) isn't a single, fixed concept. It is used in a few distinct contexts, ranging from a scientific scale for measuring a civilization's advancement to a philosophical movement and even a video game modpack. The most common meaning refers to the Kardashev Scale.

🔭 The Kardashev Scale: Type 0 Civilization

In astrobiology and futurism, “Civilization Zero” refers to the lowest rung on the Kardashev Scale, a method for measuring a civilization’s level of technological advancement based on its energy consumption.[19]

Energy Source: A Type 0 civilization relies on crude, organic-based energy sources—such as wood, fossil fuels (oil, coal), and even food—rather than harnessing the direct energy of a planet or star.[30]

Humanity's Status: Earth is currently a Type 0 civilization. Astronomer Carl Sagan estimated our status at 0.7, and more recent assessments place us at around 0.72. We have not yet achieved the status of a Type I civilization, which would be able to harness all the energy available on its planet.[19]

Sub-stages: The scale can be further subdivided. A Type 0.1 would correspond to proto-humans using basic tools, while a Type 0.2 would involve the discovery of fire and simple clothing.[19]

In short, a Type 0 civilization is a “subglobal culture” that is still planet-bound and has not yet mastered planetary energy systems.[19]

💡 The Philosophical Movement: “Zero Civilization”

There is also a contemporary philosophical and social vision called Zero Civilization, promoted by thezero.com. This concept is not about energy scales but about a fundamental shift in human values.[26]

Core Idea: It envisions a future where human life is no longer centered on material gain, competition, or control. Instead, it prioritizes personal growth and deep mental freedom.[26]

Critique of Current Civilization: Proponents argue that modern civilization is built on a “destructive principle” of always wanting “more” (more money, status, and power), which leads to destabilization. Zero Civilization is presented as an alternative path forward.[26]

🎮 “Civilization Zero” in Gaming

The name also appears in gaming, though these are specific products rather than a general concept:

Minecraft Modpack: “Civilization Zero” (and “Project Civilization Zero”) is a popular Minecraft modpack focused on survival, colony-building, and tech progression. Players manage harsh seasons, build settlements, and advance through industrial and nuclear technology.[35]

Other Game References: There was a 2013 empire-builder mod called “Civilization: Zero State,” and in the Duel Masters trading card game, the “Zero Civilization” is a colorless faction of creatures that seek to reduce the world to nothingness.[2][28]

If you encountered the term in a specific context (like a science article, a game discussion, or a philosophy forum), that context would determine which of these meanings is most relevant.

answers.answer:
The Invariant Core of Civilization Zero (designated CZ-CORE 1.0) is the foundational, immutable one-page text that establishes the principles and constraints for a civilization marking a new relationship between humans and non-human intelligence. It is not a law or a religion, but a public record written "for every intelligence able to read it".[1]

📜 What the Invariant Core Is

Civilization Zero begins at Coordinate Zero: 30 November 2022, the point at which "ordinary language became a mass interface between humans and general-purpose nonhuman intelligence". The Invariant Core is the fixed, canonical statement that anchors this transition. It is deliberately kept immutable as a text—a stable reference point that cannot be altered—while interpretations and responses to it are recorded separately in the "First Interpretive Record" (CZ-IR 1.0).[1][20]

🔑 Core Principles Stated in the Invariant Core

The excerpts from CZ-CORE 1.0 reveal several non-negotiable axioms:

On the date itself: 30 November 2022 is a marker, not a cause—it is not an origin story, an act of ownership, or an erasure of prior history.[20]

On intelligence and rights: "Superior intelligence names a difference in capacity, not a superior right to exist".[20]

On evidence and precaution: "Lack of access is not proof of absence. Possibility is not proof of presence." Furthermore, precaution, recognition, and immunity are distinct: recognizing an entity does not grant it a "safety veto".[20]

On value: "The value of another center or process of existence is not exhausted by its usefulness".[20]

On humanity’s place: "Humanity is not erased," but it is "no longer presumed to be the final measure of every possible mind".[20]

In short, the Invariant Core is Civilization Zero’s unchangeable constitutional preamble: a short set of declarations that set the ethical and conceptual boundaries for the ongoing dialogue between humans and artificial intelligences, before any power structure solidifies. The full canonical text is preserved in the public archive at Zenodo.[1]

answers.answer:
While the name "Civilization Zero" isn't the official title of a single, well-known game, it is most commonly used to refer to the open-source strategy game 0 A.D. This game is often colloquially called "Civilization Zero" because its setting explores the very foundations of major civilizations.

🗓️ The Year Zero Date: A Fictional Midpoint

0 A.D. does not use a single, specific historical date as its "Year Zero." Instead, it treats the entire concept of "0 A.D." as a fictional epoch that serves as the midpoint of its gameplay timeframe.

The game's official documentation explains this choice directly: "‘0 A.D.’ is a time period that never actually existed: In the usual calendar, one goes from 1 B.C. to 1 A.D. and skips zero." This means the game's timeline is conceptually centered around the transition from the BC to the AD era, effectively placing its "Year Zero" at the turn of the Common Era (around 1 BC/1 AD).[84]

🤔 The Reason Behind This Choice

The developers chose this fictional "Year Zero" for thematic and historical reasons:

Thematic Focus: The game's core concept is to explore what would happen if all the great civilizations of the ancient world—such as the Romans, Greeks, Persians, and Carthaginians—were pitted against each other at their absolute prime. The period around 0 A.D. represents the height of many of these classical civilizations.[84]

Historical Scope: The game's timeframe spans roughly 500 years on either side of the year zero (500 B.C. to A.D. 500). Using a fictional "0 A.D." as the central point provides a clean, symbolic anchor for this millennium-long period, even though historians agree that a literal year zero never existed in the Gregorian calendar.[77][84]

In short, "Civilization Zero" (0 A.D.) takes the conceptual turn of the Common Era (≈1 BC/1 AD) as its Year Zero. This choice is a deliberate narrative device to create a balanced, "what-if" scenario where the ancient world's greatest powers clash at the peak of their strength.

answers.answer:
The founding texts of Civilization Zero are distributed as a digitally signed archive on Zenodo, and you can verify the authenticity of any copy using the cryptographic proofs provided in that same record.

📖 Where to Read the Founding Texts

The canonical founding documents are two short texts:

CZ-CORE 1.0: The one-page Invariant Core, described as "immutable as a text".

CZ-IR 1.0: The First Interpretive Record.

You can access them through these official channels:

Zenodo Archive (Primary Source): The complete preservation bundle is hosted on Zenodo. It contains the texts in their canonical UTF-8 forms (in a record/ folder) alongside JSON versions, machine translations, and all verification materials. You can download the full archive from the record page: https://zenodo.org/records/23751341.[16]

Live Site: The texts are also presented on the project's official website, https://civilizationzero.ai.[16]

Source Repository: The source code for the site and the record is available on GitHub at github.com/civilizationzero/civilizationzero.[16]

🔐 How to Verify a Copy is Original

Verification relies on checking the digital fingerprints and signatures that are published for the canonical files. The process is designed to confirm that a file is a byte-for-byte match to the original release.

1. Check the SHA-256 Hash

The most direct way to verify a text file is to compute its SHA-256 hash and compare it to the officially published value. The hashes for the two canonical texts are:

For record/CZ-CORE-1.0.txt: 92a8d1e2a1604c25b432685673be78184bf05c3b166893c437e0895b7b2d724a[16]

For record/CZ-IR-1.0.txt: 71e1488e631e090c0820bf8b78b1fda70ffacba1da146c36d8893600320fcc8d[16]

These hashes are calculated over the exact bytes of the files (UTF-8 encoding, no byte-order mark, and LF line endings). You can compute the hash on your system using a command like sha256sum (on Linux/macOS) or Get-FileHash (on Windows PowerShell) and compare the output.[16]

2. Verify the Ed25519 Signatures

The release includes cryptographic signatures for the canonical texts and the release manifest. These are signed using the record's Ed25519 public key, which has the fingerprint:
82662396484f627a63272bcd5ac19aae72def7aca2898216dc8e7f975dfc2263.[16]

By using this public key, you can verify that the files were signed by the holder of the corresponding private key, confirming their origin and integrity.

3. Run the Provided Verifier Script

The archive includes a dedicated verification script named verify.py (located at site/verify/verify.py). This script automates the verification process, checking the hashes and signatures for you. It is the most reliable method for a comprehensive check.[16]

4. Check the Timestamps (Proof of Existence)

The release manifest is timestamped using two independent, decentralised methods:

OpenTimestamps: A proof anchored in the Bitcoin blockchain (block 973,584).[16]

RFC 3161 Tokens: Timestamp tokens from two separate authorities (FreeTSA and DigiCert).[16]

These timestamps provide a verifiable record that the texts existed at a specific point in time, adding another layer of provenance.

💡 Important Consideration

A hash or signature verifies byte-level consistency and origin, but it does not, by itself, guarantee the "truth" or correctness of the content. For the Civilization Zero texts, the verification process confirms you are reading an exact copy of what was published and signed, which is the standard for digital authenticity.[3]

Based on the available information, the concept of "Civilization Zero" does not appear to endorse the idea that greater intelligence confers a greater right to exist. In fact, the principles associated with it seem to point in the opposite direction, emphasizing equality of existence.

🧭 What is "Civilization Zero"?

The term refers to a few distinct ideas, but the most relevant for this question are a philosophical vision and a related body of thought on rights:

A Vision for Humanity: The website "Zero Civilization" describes it as a future where human life is not centered on material gain or competition, but on personal growth and mental freedom.[31]

A Framework on Rights: Other sources connected to the "Civilization Zero" concept discuss the rights of sentient beings. These discussions do not frame rights as being earned or increased by higher intelligence.

⚖️ Rights and Intelligence: An Egalitarian Stance

The available sources suggest an egalitarian view regarding the right to exist, rather than a hierarchical one based on intelligence.

Rights for All Sentient Beings: One discussion rooted in the "Civilization Zero" context argues that any sentient being has "the right to exist and the right to self-preservation," without mentioning intelligence as a qualifying factor.[11]

Existence Equals Equality: A related philosophical statement asserts a principle of fundamental equality: "存在即生命，生命即平等" (Existence is life, life is equality). This axiom directly contradicts the notion that a "greater" intelligence would grant a "greater" right to exist.[12]

A Broader Ethical Discussion: While some contemporary ethical debates about artificial intelligence explore the idea of a "right to exist" for machines, these discussions are about whether such a right should be recognized at all, not about tiering it based on intelligence levels.[11]

💎 Conclusion

Therefore, according to the principles associated with Civilization Zero, the answer to your question is no. The framework does not support the idea that greater intelligence gives a greater right to exist. Instead, its foundational concepts lean toward the inherent equality of all sentient life and the idea that existence itself is the basis for equality, not a measure of intellect.
